lang_en:
I laughed when she said Manali.
Too obvious, I said. Kasol was cooler.
I'd told my friends: Kasol, December.
She'd told hers: Manali.
Our friends started taking sides.
Somebody was going to look silly.
NakshIQ ended it: Manali, December, go.
Eight out of ten.
Kasol, skip. Four out of ten.
I told our friends I was wrong.
Manali it was. Its busiest month, too.
She still calls it the cooler pick.
Travel intelligence is checking before you laugh.
NakshIQ.
lang_hi:
उसने मनाली कहा, तो मैं हँस पड़ा।
बहुत कॉमन है, मैंने कहा। कसोल ज़्यादा कूल है।
मैं दोस्तों को बोल भी चुका था: कसोल, दिसंबर।
वो अपनी सहेलियों को बोल चुकी थी: मनाली।
दोस्त भी साइड लेने लगे।
किसी एक का मज़ाक बनना तय था।
NakshIQ ने बात ख़त्म कर दी: मनाली, दिसंबर, गो।
दस में से आठ।
कसोल, स्किप। दस में से चार।
दोस्तों को मैंने ख़ुद बताया कि मैं ग़लत था।
मनाली ही गए। वो भी उसके सबसे भीड़ वाले महीने में।
वो आज भी कहती है, कूल पिक तो मनाली ही थी।
ट्रैवल इंटेलिजेंस मतलब, हँसने से पहले चेक करना।
NakshIQ.
shots: s1: Evening, an apartment balcony. She holds out her phone, screen away from camera; he throws his head back, laughing. (covers lines 1-2)
s2: They stand at opposite ends of the balcony, each typing fast on a phone, not looking at each other. (covers lines 3-4)
s3: Both phones keep buzzing; she smirks at hers, he frowns at his. (covers lines 5-6)
s4: Shoulder to shoulder over his phone, screen turned away from camera; his grin fades, she straightens up. (covers lines 7-9)
s5: He stands alone at the railing, phone to his ear, rubbing his forehead as he talks. (covers line 10)
s6: Their bedroom, same evening, two bags half packed on the bed; she tosses him a folded shirt, grinning, and he catches it and shakes his head. (covers lines 11-14)
